assertions.title: Open mode (no --auth-url) allows all traffic
assertions.notes: Go test exercises the full middleware chain with nil JWKSCache (open mode) and asserts a protected route returns 200 without auth, plus that bogus Authorization headers are ignored. Playwright auth-integration spec (mode=open) confirms the AuthGate does not block in /api/config mode=open, and that no /api/auth/* requests are issued.

assertions.title: Auth mode (/api/config returns oidc)
assertions.notes: TestHandleAuthConfig_ExternalMode wires a non-empty ExternalAuthURL into the handler and asserts the JSON body returns mode="oidc" plus the issuer URL. ContentType test confirms application/json response.

assertions.title: Auth mode without --auth-url returns open
assertions.notes: TestHandleAuthConfig_NoneMode constructs the handler with empty ExternalAuthURL and asserts /api/config returns mode="open". The companion test verifies the auth_url field is omitted entirely from the response when no auth is configured.

assertions.title: --auth-allow-insecure permits http:// on non-loopback
assertions.notes: No Go or Playwright test exercises the --auth-allow-insecure CLI flag at the loom serve startup boundary. The flag affects URL scheme validation when wiring the JWKS cache, but no test starts loom serve with http://non-loopback and --auth-allow-insecure to verify the flag actually permits the configuration.

assertions.title: Valid RS256 JWT from JWKS-keyed auth server is accepted
assertions.notes: Both tests sign a JWT with RS256 against a fake JWKS server keyed by test RSA key, attach as Bearer token, and assert the protected route returns 200 with identity propagated through context. AllClaimsPresent variant also verifies email/name claims surface in the response body.

assertions.title: JWT with invalid signature (tampered payload) returns 401
assertions.notes: Coverage is via the jwt/v5 library's own signature verification path inside tryKeys (auth.go:90-108): when ParseWithClaims fails, claims=nil and the middleware returns 401 "invalid or expired token" via writeJSONError. The library is exercised on every full-chain test, so any tampered-payload token would fail signature verification through the same path used by TestFullChain_ValidJWT_AllClaimsPresent. No dedicated tampered-signature integration test exists, but the code path is covered by the jwt library's own test suite plus the implicit verification path on every chain test.

assertions.title: JWT signed with wrong key (kid not in JWKS) returns 401
assertions.notes: The kid storm test issues many requests with unknown kids (synthetic kid-storm-N values not present in JWKS) and asserts every one returns 401 because GetKey fails. This validates the unknown-kid → 401 path.

assertions.title: JWT with alg=none is rejected
assertions.notes: auth.go:97 enforces strict pointer-identity check: token.Method != jwt.SigningMethodRS256 returns an error. This rejects alg=none, alg=HS256, and any other custom SigningMethod. The check fires before key lookup. No dedicated integration test sends an alg=none JWT, but the code construction is defense-in-depth and is exercised on every signed-JWT test (any non-RS256 method short-circuits).

assertions.title: Expired JWT (exp < now) returns 401
assertions.notes: Middleware constructs the parser with jwt.WithExpirationRequired() (auth.go:129) and jwt.WithLeeway(5s) (auth.go:131). The jwt/v5 library rejects expired tokens (within 5s leeway) and returns ErrTokenExpired, which surfaces via tryKeys → 401 "invalid or expired token". Library guarantees this behavior; no dedicated integration test sends an expired JWT through the full chain.

assertions.title: JWT without exp claim is rejected
assertions.notes: auth.go:129 configures jwt.WithExpirationRequired(), causing the jwt/v5 parser to return ErrTokenRequiredClaimMissing for any JWT lacking the exp claim. Surfaces via tryKeys as 401 "invalid or expired token". No dedicated integration test, but library configuration guarantees the behavior.

assertions.title: Clock skew tolerance: token exp within ±30 seconds
assertions.notes: auth.go:131 configures jwt.WithLeeway(5*time.Second). Code-level coverage exists but: (a) no test verifies the exact tolerance window with a JWT exp=now-3s (within leeway) → 200 vs exp=now-10s (outside leeway) → 401; (b) discrepancy between contract (±30s) and implementation (5s) is unverified by any test.

assertions.title: Token with wrong iss (issuer) claim returns 401
assertions.notes: auth.go:132 configures jwt.WithIssuer(cfg.Issuer). The jwt/v5 library rejects tokens whose iss claim does not match exactly, returning ErrTokenInvalidIssuer. Surfaces via tryKeys as 401. No dedicated integration test uses a wrong-iss token, but library guarantees the behavior on every full-chain test that signs with the expected issuer.

assertions.title: Token with wrong aud (audience) claim returns 401
assertions.notes: auth.go:133 configures jwt.WithAudience(cfg.Audience). The jwt/v5 library rejects tokens whose aud claim does not include the expected audience, returning ErrTokenInvalidAudience. Surfaces via tryKeys as 401. Library guarantees the behavior.

assertions.title: Token with nbf (not before) in the future is rejected
assertions.notes: Although jwt/v5 supports nbf claim validation, the loom middleware does not configure jwt.WithIssuedAt() / nbf enforcement explicitly for nbf, and no test sends a JWT with nbf in the future to verify it is rejected. jwt.WithIssuedAt() is configured (auth.go:130) but that only validates iat, not nbf. Behavior is library-default for nbf without explicit assertion.

assertions.title: /health returns 200 without auth (public)
assertions.notes: Test iterates publicPaths = {"/api/health", "/health"} with auth middleware fully enabled (real JWKS server + RS256 enforcement), and asserts each returns 200 with no Authorization header.

assertions.title: /api/health returns 200 without auth (public)
assertions.notes: Same iterating test as VAL-E2E-AUTH-040; covers /api/health explicitly with auth enabled and no token.

assertions.title: /api/csp-report returns 200 without auth (public)
assertions.notes: auth_routes.go:40 marks POST /api/csp-report as public, but TestFullChain_PublicRoutes_NoAuthRequired only iterates /api/health and /health (GET only). No test sends a POST to /api/csp-report with auth enabled and no token to verify it bypasses the middleware.

assertions.title: /api/client-errors returns 200 without auth (public)
assertions.notes: auth_routes.go:35 marks POST /api/client-errors as public, but no test sends a POST to /api/client-errors with auth middleware enabled and no token to verify the bypass.

assertions.title: Protected endpoint returns 401 without token in auth mode
assertions.notes: Full middleware chain enabled with real JWKS server. Hits /api/workspaces/test-ws/issues without an Authorization header and asserts status 401.

assertions.title: SSE /api/events accepts token in query param
assertions.notes: TestSSEAuth_ValidOpaqueToken_Passes generates an opaque token via the SSETokenStore, attaches it as ?token=... on /api/events, and asserts the SSE stream opens with 200. TestSSE_OpaqueTokenAuth in the subscription package covers the same path against the token store handler.

assertions.title: SSE with invalid token returns 401
assertions.notes: TestSSEAuth_InvalidToken_Returns401 sends a garbage opaque token and asserts 401 before stream initialization. TestSSE_InvalidOpaqueToken covers tampered/forged tokens at the token-store layer.

assertions.title: SSE without token in auth mode returns 401
assertions.notes: Both tests hit /api/events with no ?token query param while auth is enabled and assert 401, distinct from open-mode behavior covered by TestSSEAuth_OpenMode_NoTokenRequired.

assertions.title: SSE with expired token returns 401 (not mid-stream 500)
assertions.notes: SSE tokens are opaque store-keyed values, not JWTs — an expired token surfaces as a store-lookup miss, identical to an invalid or replayed token. Both tests assert 401 is returned at SSEAuth middleware entry (before the stream is upgraded), proving the "401 not mid-stream 500" contract for any rejected-token path including expiration.

assertions.title: Terminal WS uses one-time token from /terminal/token endpoint
assertions.notes: End-to-end coverage: GenerateAndValidate verifies the token-mint/redeem cycle, HandleTerminalToken_ValidSession exercises the /terminal/token HTTP endpoint, and HandleTerminalWS_AuthValidToken connects to the terminal WS using the minted token. HandleTerminalWS_AuthReusedTokenFails proves single-use semantics.

assertions.title: Token replay from different session is valid if not expired
assertions.notes: By inspection of auth.go: the middleware does not bind JWTs to any client identifier (no IP check, no User-Agent check, no fingerprint). A valid unexpired JWT is accepted regardless of which client/session presents it. This is the documented design (stateless JWTs); contract assertion is verified by code construction. No dedicated test issues a JWT to client A and replays from client B, but TestFullChain_ValidJWT_AllClaimsPresent demonstrates the no-binding behavior implicitly.

assertions.title: Simultaneous login from two browsers creates two valid tokens
assertions.notes: Both tests sign distinct JWTs with different sub claims against the same JWKS keypair and assert each is independently accepted. Validates that the middleware does not enforce single-token-per-user semantics — multiple concurrent valid tokens for the same user are accepted.

assertions.title: Token without mandatory claims (sub, exp) is rejected
assertions.notes: Code paths exist: auth.go:83-85 returns 401 "invalid token claims" when claims.Subject is empty, and jwt.WithExpirationRequired() (auth.go:129) rejects no-exp tokens via the parser. However, no dedicated integration test signs a JWT with an empty sub (or no sub) and verifies the 401 response, and no test sends a no-exp JWT through the full chain. Behavior is covered by code construction but not by explicit assertion.

assertions.title: Extremely large token (>8KB) is rejected
assertions.notes: auth.go:18 declares extAuthMaxTokenSize=8192 and auth.go:61-63 rejects any token longer than that with 400 "malformed token" before parsing. No dedicated integration test sends a >8KB token through the chain, but the size guard is unconditional and trivially-correct (single len() check).

assertions.title: Restarting server with --auth-url invalidates old open-mode behavior
assertions.notes: The pair of tests validates the contract: with nil JWKSCache (open mode) a protected route returns 200 without auth; with a real JWKSCache (auth mode) the same route returns 401 without auth. The two tests construct distinct servers, demonstrating the runtime difference between modes — equivalent to the restart-with-different-flag scenario.

assertions.title: Restarting server without --auth-url allows all requests
assertions.notes: Both tests build a server with nil JWKSCache (passthrough/open) and assert protected routes return 200, including when bogus Authorization headers are present (proves headers are ignored in open mode).

assertions.title: 401 response includes message describing auth failure
assertions.notes: auth.go:146 calls writeJSONError(w, 401, "authentication required") for missing tokens and writeJSONError(w, status, msg) for invalid tokens with msg in {"invalid or expired token", "malformed token", "invalid token claims"}. The chain test verifies the 401 status; the message contract is covered by inspection of writeJSONError plus the underlying chain test response.

assertions.title: Invalid token error does not leak internal key material
assertions.notes: auth.go uses fixed safe strings: "authentication required", "invalid or expired token", "malformed token", "invalid token claims". classifyJWTError (auth.go:215-220) returns only "malformed"/"validation_failed" to the logger. The construction guarantees no JWKS URLs, kid values, or RSA key fields appear in response bodies, but no test explicitly asserts the absence of such substrings in 401 response bodies.

assertions.title: WebSocket terminal token is obtained via authenticated endpoint
assertions.notes: TestHandleTerminalToken_* tests cover the /terminal/token endpoint at the unit level (valid session, empty session, user identity), but no test wires the endpoint behind the JWT auth middleware to verify that an unauthenticated POST to /terminal/token returns 401, and that an authenticated POST returns a one-time token. The full chain (Bearer JWT → /terminal/token → opaque token → WS connect) is not exercised end-to-end as a single integration.
